response.justification: Deep and broad hands-on engineering experience (14+ years) with genuinely relevant developer-tooling work — authoring a D test runner and assertion library, building CI/CD and device-orchestration infrastructure, and teaching test automation courses — makes the technical half of this role a strong match. However, the resume shows no formal people-management track record: all titles are individual-contributor (Senior/Staff Engineer) with no evidence of direct reports, performance reviews, or one-on-ones, which is a hard minimum for this Level II Manager role. Mobile-platform depth is also thin and dated (iOS/Apple TV work in 2015-16), and recent work skews to web/full-stack product engineering rather than large-scale build systems. Worth a screening call to probe informal leadership at Altom, GISCollective, and re:cinq, but the management gap is material.
strengths: Authentic developer-tools depth: test runner, assertion library, CI/CD and DevOps infrastructure
14+ years across web, mobile, desktop, embedded; strong TDD/craftsmanship and code-quality culture
Proven knowledge-sharing: workshops, multi-module Selenium course, conference talks, OSS founder
concerns: No demonstrated people management — misses the 2-year direct-report minimum
Mobile-platform exposure is limited and roughly a decade old
No evidence of roadmap ownership, org-level change leadership, or cross-team alignment at scale

key_factors.factor: Developer tooling and test infrastructure expertise
